source_text: These findings agree with previous studies that found the fecal microbiota of teens to be more similar to that of their parents than to unrelated adults

claim: Multiplex DNA sequencing was performed with an Illumina GAIIx instrument located in the Center for Genome Sciences and Systems Biology at Washington University School of Medicine.
source_text: Multiplex DNA sequencing was performed with a Illumina GAIIx instrument located in the Center for Genome Sciences and Systems Biology at Washington University School of Medicine
evidence_reasoning: This describes the sequencing methodology and location.

claim: A permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) was used to determine whether communities differ significantly between families.
source_text: We used a permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) using the PERMANOVA+ add on (Anderson et al. 2008) to Plymouth Routines In Multivariate Ecological Research (PRIMER v6) package (Clarke and Gorley, 2006). The PERMANOVA analysis was based on the unweighted UniFrac dissimilarity matrix, type III partial sums of squares, and 999 random permutations of the residuals under the reduced model to determine whether communities differ significantly between families
evidence_reasoning: This describes the statistical methodology used in the study.

claim: An analysis similar to ANOSIM was used to test the hypothesis that within-family communities are more similar than between-family communities.
source_text: We then used a custom script for an analysis similar to an analysis of similarities (ANOSIM) in R version 2.13.2 (R Development Core Team, 2011) to test the hypothesis that within-family communities are more similar than between-family communities
evidence_reasoning: This describes the statistical methodology used to test a specific hypothesis.

claim: Significance levels were calculated by comparing the R statistic against the distribution generated from 10,000 permutations of the randomized dataset.
source_text: Significance levels were calculated by comparing the R statistic against the distribution generated from 10,000 permutations of the randomized dataset

claim: A distance-based linear model analysis with 999 permutations was used to determine whether age, gender, pet ownership, and family size explain differences in community composition.
source_text: To determine whether age, gender, pet ownership, and family size (i.e., cohabitation of children) explain differences in community composition, we used a distance-based linear model analysis with 999 permutations using the package DistLM in the PERMANOVA+ add-on to PRIMER
evidence_reasoning: This describes the statistical methodology for testing multiple factors.

claim: Model selection was based on Akaike's Information Criterion with a second order bias correction (AICc).
